title: sessionStorage
explain: sessionStorage has the same API as localStorage but a narrower scope: one namespace per origin and per tab, and it disappears when the tab closes. I use it for state that belongs to one working session in one tab, such as a multi-step form draft or an OAuth state value across a redirect.
model:
**sessionStorage ≈ origin + tab.** Same API as [localStorage](#/sd/f/local-storage) (synchronous strings, about 5 MB), narrower scope and lifetime.

| Situation | Still there? |
|---|---|
| Reload the tab | yes |
| Navigate to another page of the same origin in that tab | yes |
| Open a new tab to the same page by typing the URL | no, starts empty |
| Close the tab, then reopen the site | no, gone |
| Same page in two tabs | separate copies |
| Different origin or an iframe from another origin | separate store |

Duplicating a tab, or `window.open` without `noopener`, copies the data once; afterwards the two diverge. Some browsers restore it with a restored tab; do not rely on that. It is never sent to the server and is readable by any script on that origin.

**Use for:** a multi-step form draft, scroll position, a per-tab selection, an OAuth `state` or PKCE verifier across the IdP round trip. **Do not use** for anything that must outlive the tab or be shared across tabs.

details.q: A value is written in a tab on https://shop.example.com/cart. When is it still readable?
details.a: After a reload, and after following a link to /checkout in the same tab. Not in a brand-new tab even for the same URL, and not after closing the tab and reopening the site.

details.q: Two tabs edit two order drafts stored as `localStorage['draft']` and overwrite each other. Fix?
details.a: Keep each tab's draft in sessionStorage, which is per tab; or key the draft by order id in localStorage if it must also outlive the tab. Per-tab state belongs in per-tab storage.

details.q: Why store an OAuth PKCE code verifier in sessionStorage rather than localStorage before redirecting to the IdP?
details.a: It is only needed in this tab for the redirect round trip. Scoping it to the tab keeps parallel logins in other tabs apart, and it disappears with the tab instead of lingering. See [IdP](#/sd/f/idp).
Only in lifetime and scope. Any script on the origin can still read it, so XSS can steal what it holds. It is also never sent to the server. Do not treat it as secure storage for long-lived secrets.

details.q: What happens to it across a page reload or a link opened with a new tab?
details.a: A reload keeps it. A link opened in a new tab starts empty, except when the tab was opened by `window.open` without `noopener`, where it is copied once at creation and then diverges.

details.q: Place cookie, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB on one line each.
details.a: Cookie: sent to the server per request, expiry set by the server or session-only. localStorage: per origin, persistent, scripts only, never sent. sessionStorage: per origin and per tab, gone when the tab closes, scripts only. IndexedDB: per origin, persistent (best-effort eviction), asynchronous and large, scripts only.

prompts.q: Explain sessionStorage scope and lifetime against localStorage.
points: Gone when the tab closes; new tab starts empty

prompts.q: Choose the storage for: a theme preference, a multi-step checkout draft, a PKCE verifier, a session ID.
points: Checkout draft: sessionStorage, or localStorage keyed by id if it must persist

prompts.q: Compare the four browser storages on scope, lifetime and who can read them.
points: Cookie: sent to the server, readable by server
localStorage and sessionStorage: scripts only, never sent
